Subject: Evaluation: pricing alignment & migration path to Redwood

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency and the observability features. We are currently evaluating a move from our incumbent vendor (LiveServe) and need to understand whether Redwood can meet both an economic parity ask and a low-risk migration path.

Two asks to start:
- Can you provide an apples-to-apples pricing comparison against our current committed spend (attached is a Q3 usage snapshot).
- What sort of migration/onboarding credits and timeline do you typically offer for a 12–24 month commitment?

Constraints: procurement is focused on either price parity or a clear offset (credits + free pilot) that nets to parity in year 1. Also need commitment around data residency and an SLA uplift.

Attached: beacon-q3-usage-snapshot.xlsx (anonymized token and request volumes).

Elena

BeaconHealth

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and for the usage file. I looped in Jordan (commercial lead) and Connor (solutions) so we can pull together an economic comparison and a migration plan that addresses parity.

High level we can do two concrete paths:
1) Hosted parity path: list-discount + onboarding credit to meet your year-1 economic target; 30-day pilot at reduced runtime rate to validate latency and cost.
2) Dedicated reserved path: slightly higher baseline but lower unit cost at scale + prioritized support + SLA uplift; we'll propose credits to offset initial delta.

Next steps: Jordan suggested we model both with your Q3 numbers and come back with a single-sheet comparison and a recommended package (commit term, credits, pilot period, and migration milestones). Can you confirm the incumbent's effective discounted unit price today (or the contract line we should match)?

I attached a draft retention offer (redwood-retention-offer-v3.pdf) — internal pricing placeholders only. We will replace with firm numbers after internal alignment. Proposed time to sync: Monday or Tuesday next week?

— Hannah

Hi Hannah — thanks. We want to be explicit so procurement has a clear negotiating point. The incumbent effective price after discounts is approximately $0.0009 per token equivalent (avg) today; annualized committed spend ~ $850,000.

Procurement's posture: they will only consider a move if either:
- Redwood can match or beat the incumbent effective unit economics in year 1 including any migration overhead, OR
- Redwood provides a combination of onboarding credits + a guaranteed pilot that reduces net cost to parity for the first 12 months.

Security/legal have called out the need for data residency confirmation (US-only) and a 99.95% uptime SLA for production.

If you can send a firm playbook (numbers) and a sample statement of work / migration timeline, we can take it to the steering committee this Thursday.

Elena

Hannah / team — thanks. Quick internal proposal to present:

Assumptions (from Elena): annualized committed spend target $850k; incumbent effective $0.0009/token-eq.

Commercial offer (option A - Hosted parity path):
- Term: 12 months committed
- Unit price: $0.00085/token-eq (net effective price) if they commit to $850k ARR
- Onboarding credit: $60,000 applied over Q1 to offset migration egress and initial infra delta
- Pilot: 60-day pilot at 50% of the unit rate (to validate latency/ops)
- SLA: 99.95% for production routes; 24/7 support during migration window

Commercial offer (option B - Dedicated reserved path):
- Term: 24 months committed
- Unit price: $0.00078/token-eq after reserved discount
- One-time migration credit: $40,000 + waived first-month dedicated capacity fee
- Commitment to US-only residency on dedicated pool + SOC2 evidence

Other levers: volume tiers, prepay credits, and a refundable performance guarantee tied to go-live milestones. Recommend presenting option A as the procurement-friendly path and option B as the long-term cost-optimized path.

Attachments to include: BH-offer-2026-05.xlsx (single-sheet econ + credit application), updated redwood-retention-offer-v3.pdf (with firm numbers).

If they push for full parity without credits, we'll need to either deepen the discount or expand a usage-based rebate tied to observed month-1 throughput.

Jordan
